claim: Windsor Castle 2026 ticket prices: adult £32 advance/£36 same-day, young person (18-24) £21/£24, child (5-17) £16/£18, under-5 free; castle operates 10:00–17:15 with last admission 16:00.
quote: Adults (25+): £32 advance / £36 on-the-day ... Young persons (18-24): £21 advance / £24 ... Children (5-17): £16 advance / £18 ... 10:00 – 17:15 (last admission 16:00)

claim: Windsor Castle is closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays and as a working palace can close at short notice; tickets cheaper booked in advance and £1 tickets are available for those on Universal Credit during certain months.
quote: Windsor Castle is closed on Tuesdays and Wednesdays but as a working palace it can close on other days and at short notice ... £1 tickets are available for those on Universal Credit

claim: Changing the Guard at Windsor takes place at 11:00 in the Lower Ward, provisionally Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays in 2026, with no ceremony on Sundays and possible cancellation in wet weather.
quote: Provisionally the Windsor Castle Guard are expected to change on Tuesday's, Thursday's, and Saturday's in 2026. The Changing the Guard Ceremony takes place in the Lower Ward inside Windsor Castle at 11:00am

claim: Queen Elizabeth II is interred in the King George VI Memorial Chapel off the North Quire aisle at St George's Chapel, viewable when the Castle is open (not Sundays); chapel access is included in a Windsor Castle ticket and photography inside is forbidden.

claim: Eton College Heritage Tours are suspended for all of 2026 due to essential building works, but the three museums (Antiquities, Eton Life, Natural History) remain free to the public on Sunday afternoons 1:30–4:00pm.
quote: there will be no Heritage Tours in 2026 due to essential building works ... the three museums remain accessible on Sunday afternoons from 1:30–4:00 PM

claim: Savill Garden 2026 admission: £14.95 adult advance / £18.95 same-day, £6.50 child (5–15) advance, carers and under-5s free; 35-acre garden with free parking included with paid entry, postcode TW20 0UJ.
quote: Adult: £14.95 ... Adult: £18.95 ... Child (5-15): £6.50 ... Carer: Free ... 35 acres within Windsor Great Park. Use postcode TW20 0UJ ... Free parking is included with paid entry

claim: Windsor Great Park is free to enter daily; charges apply only to parking, the Savill Garden, Adventure Play and Wildlife Trust activities, and parking is free with paid entry to Savill Garden or Adventure Play.
quote: Windsor Great Park itself is free to enter daily ... Parking is free with a paid visit to The Savill Garden and Adventure Play

claim: The Long Walk runs 2.64 miles (4.2 km) from the George IV Gateway at Windsor Castle to the Copper Horse statue of George III on Snow Hill; the round trip is over 5 miles and takes roughly 90 minutes at average walking pace.
quote: the long walk measures 2.64 miles in length ... 2.64 miles (4.2 km) each way ... cover more than 5 miles (8.4km) in total ... allow yourselves at least an hour and a half

claim: Frogmore House and Garden opens to the public only on three annual Charity Garden Open Days, with 2026 dates of 7, 8 and 9 June supporting the National Garden Scheme, Blind Veterans UK and Battersea Dogs & Cats Home; pre-booked groups of 15+ can also visit in August.
quote: Frogmore House and Garden will open to the public on 7, 8 and 9 June 2026, as part of the annual Charity Garden Open Days. The beneficiaries of this year's opening will be The National Garden Scheme, Blind Veterans UK and Battersea Dogs & Cats Home

claim: Frogmore House sits about half a mile south of Windsor Castle in the Home Park and its grounds include Queen Victoria and Prince Albert's Royal Mausoleum (closed to the public) plus picturesque 1790s gardens with a Gothic-ruin summerhouse by James Wyatt.
quote: Frogmore House stands approximately half a mile south of Windsor Castle in Windsor Home Park ... Queen Victoria and Prince Albert's mausoleum dominates the grounds, completed in 1868 ... the mausoleum remains closed to the public

claim: The Crooked House of Windsor (Market Cross House) at 51 High Street dates from c. 1687, is Grade II listed and now operates as a tea-room famous for its leaning facade caused by reconstruction with unseasoned green oak.
quote: a commercial building in Windsor, England, dating from c. 1687, and is the oldest teahouse in England and Grade II listed ... using unseasoned green oak instead of a tougher wood and as the wood started to dry out, the building started to lean

claim: Windsor is served by two stations (Windsor & Eton Central and Windsor & Eton Riverside), both a few minutes' walk from the Castle; from Maidenhead/Bray, travellers change at Slough for a 6-minute branch line to Windsor & Eton Central via GWR.
quote: Windsor is served by two train stations: Windsor and Eton Central and Windsor and Eton Riverside, both situated within a few minutes' walk of Windsor Castle ... change trains at Slough to catch the 6-minute branch line service to Windsor and Eton Central

claim: Bray village is about 6 miles / 10 minutes by car from Windsor town centre.
quote: The driving distance between Bray and Windsor is 6 miles, taking approximately 10 minutes to drive

claim: Henley-on-Thames is roughly 11 miles by road from Bray, about a 16-minute drive.
quote: The driving distance between Henley-on-Thames to Bray, Berkshire is 11 miles. It takes approximately 16 min to drive from Henley-on-Thames to Bray, Berkshire.

claim: Henley is a 'Town of Festivals' with 300+ historically significant buildings including St Mary's Church, the Town Hall and Henley Bridge, and is famous for the Royal Regatta.
quote: Henley attracts visitors through several unique attractions... the world's greatest rowing regatta... Among its 300 historically significant buildings are St Mary's Church, the Town Hall, and Henley Bridge, with many Georgian frontages covering older buildings.

claim: Henley's River & Rowing Museum closed on 21 September 2025 after trustees cited financial pressures, so it is no longer a 2026 day-trip draw.
quote: On 27 February, 2025, the trustees of the museum announced that the museum was to cease operations and close, due to financial pressures.

claim: The Hambleden Mill to Henley circular is a 6.1-mile (about 3-hour) Thames-side walk taking in Hambleden Lock, Temple Island and Fawley Court — said to have inspired Toad Hall in The Wind in the Willows.
quote: Fawley Court: A Grade I listed house from 1684, reportedly 'the inspiration for Toad Hall in Kenneth Graham's The Wind in the Willows.'

claim: Marlow is roughly 7 road-miles from Bray, around a 15–20 minute drive.
quote: The distance between Marlow and Bray, Berkshire is 10 miles as the crow flies, with a road distance of 7 miles. Most sources confirm this drive time is approximately 15-20 minutes under normal traffic conditions.

claim: Marlow is positioned as 'England's riverside gastronomic hub', home to Tom Kerridge's Hand & Flowers — the UK's only two-Michelin-star pub — and a six-mile Marlow Circular Walk through the Chilterns.
quote: England's riverside gastronomic hub... The Hand & Flowers stands out as 'the UK's only two-Michelin-star pub'... The Marlow Circular Walk is a six-mile route through Chilterns landscapes.

claim: Marlow's signature sights include the elegant 1832 William Tierney Clark suspension bridge linking Buckinghamshire and Berkshire, and All Saints Church on the riverbank.
quote: an elegant suspension bridge built in 1832... designed by William Tierney Clark and linking the counties of Buckinghamshire and Berkshire.

claim: The Macdonald Compleat Angler is a 400-year-old riverside country house hotel at Marlow Bridge, a few minutes' walk from the high street.
quote: The Macdonald Compleat Angler is an elegant, 400-year-old country house in the heart of Marlow, with the high street just a few minutes' walk away and the river snaking beautifully around its grounds.

claim: Cookham's Stanley Spencer Gallery opens daily 10:30–16:30 in summer (from 4 April 2026), with adult admission £9 and a free 'Revealing Genius' workbook plus Bloomberg Connects audio guide.
quote: Open Every Day 10:30am – 4:30pm... Adults pay £9.00 (or £10.00 with donation)... The gallery provides a complimentary 'Revealing Genius' workbook with 'questions, drawing prompts, and close-looking activities'.

claim: Cookham sits about 4 miles from Bray, with Maidenhead almost exactly at the midpoint between the two villages.
quote: The distance between Cookham and Bray is 4 miles... the geographic midpoint between Bray and Cookham is Maidenhead, which is 0.57 miles away from the midpoint.

claim: Boulter's Lock at Maidenhead — rebuilt in 1912 after the Thames Conservancy bought Ray Mill Island in 1909 — is a Victorian/Edwardian boating landmark and a popular kayaking site with a summer canoe flume.
quote: The Thames Conservancy purchased Ray Mill Island in 1909 and rebuilt the lock in 1912, creating its present form... Currently serves as a premier whitewater kayaking venue with seasonal flume installations.

claim: Cliveden, the National Trust estate above Maidenhead, has 80 acres of formal gardens within 375 acres of woodland, with the Cliveden Reach 'one of the prettiest stretches of the river' and boating from 27 March to October 2026.
quote: 80 acres of year-round interest and colour... 375 acres of woodlands, riverbank and formal gardens... Soak up one of the prettiest stretches of the river, Cliveden Reach. The perfect spot for a picnic or a stroll.

claim: Eton High Street, opposite Windsor across the Thames footbridge, is a mile-long parade of independent retailers running down to Eton College.
quote: a fine selection of independent retailers committed to personal service and individual attention, from wining and dining to gifts for men and women.

claim: The Eton Walkway is a 2-mile, one-hour circular linking 18 bronze-marker points of interest including Eton College, the Burning Bush, the Antony Gormley statue and the Brocas riverside meadow.
quote: The Eton Walkway is a 2-mile / one-hour circular walk that connects 18 points of interest in the town starting at Windsor Bridge... The 18 shields mark: The King's Stables, the Cockpit, Porny School, Baldwin's Bridge, Eton College, the Burning Bush... the Gormley Statue... the Brocas and Eton Boat House.

claim: The Mill at Sonning is a dinner-theatre venue combining a 215-seat theatre, restaurant and Waterwheel Bar in a converted ~1800 flour mill on a Thames island; the 2026 season includes 'Anything Goes' and 'Shear Madness'.
quote: THEATRE | RESTAURANT | WATERWHEEL BAR... The 2026 season features productions such as 'Jack and Sarah,' 'Anything Goes,' and 'Shear Madness'.

claim: The Bull Inn at Sonning is a 600-year-old Grade II-listed timber-framed pub in the heart of the village and a popular Thames Path walkers' stop.
quote: The Bull Inn, Sonning, in Berkshire is a historic Grade 2 listed timber-framed pub and hotel that is more than 600 years old... a popular stop with walkers of the Thames Path too, being just a few steps from the river.

claim: Wallingford — at the outer edge of the 30 km range — offers the ruins of William the Conqueror's 1067 castle, a 19-arch medieval Thames bridge, Wallingford Museum and Agatha Christie heritage trails.
quote: the remains and gardens of the medieval Wallingford Castle, built by William the Conqueror in 1067... Wallingford Bridge, a stunning medieval landmark spanning the River Thames... the long term home of Agatha Christie.

claim: Cliveden's estate is open daily 9:30am–5pm with house visits running Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays from 2 March to 29 October 2026, in 30-minute slots from 11:00–12:30 booked first-come at the Information Centre.
quote: From 2 March to 29 October 2026, house visits run every Monday, Tuesday and Thursday starting every 10 minutes from 11:00am-12:30pm and last 30-minutes. Tickets are available (on a first come, first served basis) from the Information Centre.

claim: Cliveden lies about 10 miles (16 km) from Bray and only 2 miles from Maidenhead.
quote: The distance between Bray, Berkshire and Cliveden is 10 miles. Cliveden House is located just 2 miles from the riverside town of Maidenhead.

claim: Hughenden Manor near High Wycombe is the former home of Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli, with Italianate parterre gardens and rooms recreated as Disraeli knew them; the site also hosted the WWII top-secret 'Hillside' bombing-map operation.
quote: Hughenden is the former home of Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli and features formal Italianate-style gardens with Victorian parterre... During the 1940s, Hughenden was the site of a top-secret operation, codenamed Hillside...

claim: Dorney Court, a Grade I Tudor manor c.1440 home to the Palmer family for 450 years, opens to the public only on 4 & 25 May, every afternoon in June and 31 August 2026, 12:30–16:00; adult £13, concessions £11, child (10–16) £7.50.
quote: In 2026, unrestricted, public, opening when all visitors are welcome without reservation falls upon 4 & 25 May; every afternoon in June and 31 August (all 1230 – 1600). Adult: £13.00 Concessions: £11.00 Children (10 -16): £7.50

claim: Stonor Park, four miles north of Henley-on-Thames, is the seat of a recusant Catholic family where Edmund Campion's Decem Rationes was secretly printed in 1581; the chapel sustained local Catholic worship through the penal era.
quote: In 1581, the Jesuit priests Edmund Campion and Robert Parsons lived and worked at Stonor Park, and Campion's Decem Rationes was printed here on a secret press... the Stonors remained Roman Catholic throughout the 17th and 18th centuries...

claim: Stonor House, Chapel, Gardens and Pantry Café operate on a published 2026 opening calendar (with closures such as 20 April 2026); the estate also includes the Tumblestone Hollow adventure area.
quote: Stonor Park and Gardens in Oxfordshire with Tumblestone Hollow

claim: Greys Court near Henley-on-Thames opens the house 11:00–16:00 and garden 10:00–16:00, with last entry one hour before closing (30 minutes for the house).
quote: The House is open from 11:00am to 4:00pm, the Garden from 10:00am to 4:00pm... The last entry to the site is one hour before closing. The last entry to the house is 30 minutes before house closure.

claim: Basildon Park is an 18th-century Palladian mansion designed by John Carr (1776–1783) for Sir Francis Sykes, rescued by Lord and Lady Iliffe in the 1950s and given to the National Trust in 1978; it stood in for Netherfield in the 2005 Pride & Prejudice.
quote: The house was built between 1776 and 1783 for Sir Francis Sykes and designed by John Carr in the Palladian style... In 1978, the Iliffes presented the property to the National Trust...

claim: West Wycombe Park, a Palladian Dashwood family seat, opens 1 April–27 August 2026 with the house from 2 June; weekday house access is guided-tour only (tickets first-come from 2pm) and Sundays are free-flow.
quote: West Wycombe Park is open from the 1st of April through to the 27th of August 2026. The House opens from the 2nd of June... The House is accessed by guided tour only on weekdays, and is free flow on Sundays.

claim: Englefield House (private residence, gardens only) opens Mondays year-round and Tuesday–Thursday April–October; admission is £5 adult via honesty box, children free.
quote: The gardens are open every Monday from April-September (10am-6pm) and October-March (10am-4pm). Additionally, gardens are also open Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday from April to October... It costs £5 for adults to enter the garden, with children going free.

claim: Mapledurham House, an Elizabethan mansion on the Oxfordshire/Berkshire Thames border, is currently closed to the public with tours only on selected dates listed on the estate site.
quote: Mapledurham House and Grounds is currently closed to the public.

claim: Frogmore House, a Royal Residence since 1792 in Windsor Home Park, opens to individuals only on three summer Charity Open Days per year, with pre-booked groups of 15+ admitted in August.
quote: Frogmore House is only open to individuals on three summer Charity Open Days each year, when all proceeds are donated to specially selected charities. Frogmore is also open to pre-booked groups of 15 people or more during August only.

claim: Non-member adult entry to Cliveden's grounds and gardens is £21.85 (child £10.93) at the 2026 group entry rate, with National Trust members free.

claim: Thames Path Henley to Marlow is 8.7 miles (14 km) passing Temple Island, Hambleden Lock and Mill, Hurley and Bisham Church; Marlow to Windsor is 14.3 miles via Bourne End, Cookham, Cliveden Reach and Boulter's Lock.
quote: Day 1: Henley-on-Thames to Marlow Distance: 8.7 miles / 14 km ... Hambleden Lock ... Day 2: Marlow to Windsor Distance: 14.3 miles / 23 km ... Cookham ... Boulter's Lock ... Cliveden Estate

claim: The Henley to Marlow section is described as one of the most scenic and quintessentially English stretches of the Thames Path, with gentle level paths and Hambleden Lock reached after about 3 miles.
quote: walking downstream from Henley-on-Thames to Marlow offers riverside inns, wooden footbridges, lush meadows and postcard-perfect villages. It's a gentle walk on mainly level paths ... After around 3 miles, you reach Hambleden Lock

claim: Coombe Hill is the highest viewpoint in the Chiltern Hills at 260m (852 ft), offering panoramic views over the Aylesbury Vale and on clear days as far as the Cotswolds, on a moderately energetic circular trail past Chequers.
quote: At 260m (852 feet) above sea level, Coombe Hill is the highest viewpoint in the Chiltern Hills, affording panoramic views over the Aylesbury Vale, and on a clear day you can see as far as the Cotswolds.

claim: The Whiteleaf and Chequers Circular is the top-rated Chilterns walk (4.7 stars, 1,663 reviews on AllTrails), taking in Whiteleaf Hill Nature Reserve and the 1742-recorded chalk Whiteleaf Cross.
quote: the Whiteleaf and Chequers Circular is rated 4.7 stars from 1,663 reviews ... Whiteleaf Cross is a chalk hill figure first recorded in 1742

claim: French Brothers run Windsor public Thames cruises with a 40-minute round trip (Adult £13.50) and 2-hour round trip (Adult £22), departing daily every 30 minutes from 10am-5pm 11 February to 29 October from Windsor Promenade.
quote: 40-Minute Round Trip: Adult £13.50 ... 2-Hour Round Trip: Adult £22 ... 11 February to 29 October: Daily – every 30 minutes from 10am to 5pm

claim: Hobbs of Henley, a family-run business with over 150 years of experience and the largest fleet on the Thames, hires self-drive Pilot Class diesel boats, Pearly Class outboard launches and luxury Linssen cruisers by the hour, day or week.

claim: Paddleboard Maidenhead, established 2014, operates from Ray Mill Island with British Canoeing level 3 coaches running lessons, SUP Club sessions and Thames paddleboarding trips.
quote: A family-run business established in 2014, operating from Ray Mill Island ... British Canoeing level 3 coaches for Thames paddleboarding trips, SUP Club and lessons

claim: Moose Canoe and SUP Hire is based at Bisham Abbey near Marlow and hires Canadian canoes, sit-on-top kayaks and SUPs along the River Thames.

claim: Henley Canoe Hire offers canoe, kayak and SUP rentals on the Thames from 1-hour up to half-day and full-day paddles with custom adventure packages.

claim: The Cliveden estate has 375 acres of woodlands, riverbank and formal gardens with several waymarked walking trails offering views over the Thames; National Trust membership or admission fee required.

claim: Caversham Boat Services in Reading hires self-drive day boats including the 12-person Montego, with options to cruise west towards Goring or east towards Henley and tuition provided on the day.

quote: Minifigure Speedway... Put the pedal to the metal and then slam it in reverse, who will be first across the finish line?... LEGO City Driving School... Earn your first driving licence at LEGO City Driving School!

claim: Legoland Windsor 2026 uses dynamic pricing; off-peak day tickets can be as low as £32 (Mar–Oct), and annual passes start at £64 per person.

claim: Bray sits roughly 3.2 miles (~5 km) from Legoland Windsor Resort, making it the closest major theme park to the village.
quote: Bray is 3.2 miles from LEGOLAND Windsor Resort.

claim: Bekonscot Model Village (Beaconsfield, ~25 km from Bray) charges £15.00 adult / £9.50 child for 2026, with 10% off when booked at least 48 hours ahead online; it bills itself as the world's oldest original model village (1929) depicting 1930s rural England across 1.5 acres.

quote: Adults: £17.50, Children: £15.50, Seniors: £16.50... all tickets are +£2.00 if bought on the day of visiting.

claim: Odds Farm Park (near High Wycombe, ~18 km from Bray) combines rare-breed farm animals, outdoor sand/water/mini-golf play and a giant indoor soft-play barn, open daily year-round with seasonal dinosaur weekends and adult farm nights.
quote: Whatever the Season and whatever the weather... rare breed animals with daily interactive activities... dinosaur weekends, adult farm nights, and seasonal celebrations

claim: Odds Farm Park standard pricing runs roughly £13.50 adult, £12.50 child (2-16), £4.95 toddler (1-2), under-1s free; site is cashless and pre-booking required.
quote: children aged 1-2 requiring a nominal £4.95 ticket, and children under 1 visiting free of charge... standard tickets for children aged 2-16 are £12.50 and standard tickets for adults are £13.50

claim: The Look Out Discovery Centre (Bracknell, ~22 km from Bray) charges adults £5.55–£11.10, children £4.10–£8.20 and family savers £15.20–£30.40 depending on date; under-3s and carers are free.
quote: Adult: £5.55 to £11.10, Child: £4.10 to £8.20, Saver Family Ticket: £15.20 to £30.40... free admission for children under 3 and carers

claim: The Look Out runs 90+ hands-on science exhibits inside Swinley Forest woodland and requires pre-booked timed sessions; the lift is currently out of service.
quote: over 90 hands-on science activities which children of all ages can enjoy... The lift in the discovery centre exhibition is currently out of service

claim: Thames Valley Adventure Playground in Taplow (3 km from Bray) is a 2.5-acre inclusive play charity for children and adults with disabilities, featuring sensory room, soft play, crazy golf, zip wires and adapted bikes; suggested contribution £14/session or £20 all day, carers free.
quote: 2.5 acres of inclusive play facilities including a multi-sensory room, giant soft play, crazy golf, castle climbing and specially adapted bikes... The suggested contribution is £14 per user for a single session, and £20 for an all day session

claim: Coral Reef Waterworld in Bracknell (~22 km) is the local water park with flumes and wave features; published prices are £18.60 adult, £13.20 child, £1.20 under-5s and spectators, with 5 hours of free parking on registration plate.
quote: £13.20 for kids, £18.60 for adults (16+), £1.20 for under 5s, £1.20 for spectators... 5 hours of free parking when they provide their vehicle registration

claim: California Country Park near Wokingham (~25 km from Bray) offers free entry to 100 acres of heath and bog, with adventure playground, sensory garden, zip wire, paddling pool, fishing on Longmoor Lake and Jacksons Cafe.
quote: Play area including water play, tree houses, woodland adventure trail, Sensory Garden... zip wire course is absolutely unmissable... Fishing at Longmoor Lake

claim: Dinton Pastures (Wokingham, ~25 km) is a 350-acre free-entry country park with adventure playground, adventure golf, disc golf, sailing, paddlesports and pond-dipping aimed at ages 2–adult through its Activity Centre.
quote: 350-acre country park... award-winning adventure play area... sailing to bushcraft and paddlesport to pond dipping, catering for a range of ages from two year olds to adults

claim: Golden Tours hop-on hop-off open-top bus tour of Windsor and Eton runs March–November with 11 stops and a 24-hour ticket priced from £16 adult, £9 child (5-15), £13 senior/student, £40 family (2+2).
quote: 24-hour ticket prices are from; Adult £16.00, Child (5-15) £9.00, Senior/Student £13.00, Family (2+2) £40.00... Hop-on, hop-off tours of Windsor operate March to November

claim: ZSL Whipsnade Zoo sits 38 driving miles (~61 km) from Windsor and so falls well outside the 30 km Bray radius — exclude from a Bray weekend shortlist.
quote: The driving distance between Whipsnade Zoo and Windsor is 38 miles, and it takes approximately 49 minutes to drive.

claim: Royal Ascot 2026 runs 16-20 June with Windsor Enclosure tickets from £37, Queen Anne from £99 and a members-only Royal Enclosure.

claim: Royal Ascot's Royal Enclosure dress code requires hats/headpieces with a 10cm base, no strapless or off-the-shoulder dresses, and skirts not far above the knee.

claim: The Royal Windsor Horse Show 2026 takes place 14-17 May in the private Home Park beside Windsor Castle, with general entry from £28.
quote: Royal Windsor Horse Show is taking place from Thursday 14th to Sunday 17th May 2026. General entry starts from £28, family tickets from £25, and group tickets (10+) from £23.

claim: Henley Royal Regatta 2026 runs Tuesday 30 June to Sunday 5 July, with over 400 races and a public Regatta Enclosure plus the members-only Stewards' Enclosure.

claim: Henley Festival 2026 runs Wednesday 8 to Sunday 12 July on the Regatta site, with a 2026 lineup including Boy George & Culture Club, Sugababes, Ezra Collective and Lulu.

claim: The Cartier Queen's Cup at Guards Polo Club, Smith's Lawn in Windsor Great Park, holds its semi-finals on Wednesday 10 June and the final on Sunday 14 June 2026.
quote: The Cartier Queen's Cup will be held on the Semi-Finals on Wednesday June 10, and the Final on Sunday, June 14, 2026 ... the jewel in the crown of English polo.

claim: HPA International Day for the Royal Salute Coronation Cup is on Saturday 25 July 2026 at Guards Polo Club, with England defending the cup against an international team.
quote: HPA's International Day will take place on Saturday, 25th July 2026 at Guards Polo Club ... England squad will be at their peak in a bid to retain the mighty Coronation Cup.

claim: Royal County of Berkshire Polo Club's 2026 highlights include the Justerini & Brooks Prince of Wales Trophy final on 16 May and the John Prestwich final on 13 June, with most matches free to walk up to.
